name: Refundable Deposit Pre-Order
phase: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
hypothesis: We believe users will pay [Price Y] for our forthcoming product. We will verify this by running a pre-order campaign with a required, refundable $50 reservation deposit, and consider it validated if ≥ 3.0% of unique page visitors complete the checkout transaction.
schematic: Payment at step 2 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: State the product is in development and offer priority queue placement for a refundable deposit.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Drive qualified traffic to the reservation page and process real payments via a gateway.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Measure payment completion, refunds requested, and checkout questions.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Build a checkout flow that clearly states the product is in active development, offering priority queue placement in exchange for a refundable deposit.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Drive qualified traffic to the reservation page and process real financial transactions via a payment gateway.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Measure payment completion rates, refund requests, and customer questions submitted during checkout.

warning.label: Frictionless Refund Psychology
warning.text: When deposits are low and refundable, buyers treat checkout as a bookmark rather than a commitment.

warningFull: When deposits are low, fully refundable, and clearly framed as risk-free, conversion rates often artificially inflate, as buyers treat the checkout as an easy way to bookmark the product rather than an actual purchase commitment.
